contentModel.scope: Every content object carries {module, chapter, lesson}. Absent levels are null. The Library groups papers by it. It is no longer used for an edge rail — that feature is cancelled.
contentModel.notes: Private. Yours only. {lessonId, t, body} — body may be empty, a bare pin is allowed and is the point. Never has replies. Never visible to anyone else.
contentModel.threads: One table. lessonId + t set = a comment: appears under that video AND in People. lessonId null = a module post: People only, never under a video. This asymmetry is the whole rule and it enforces itself.
contentModel.replies: Belong to a thread, never to a moment. One mark per thread, at the moment it was asked. Replies get no marks and no timestamps of their own.
contentModel.quizQuestions: Three options, labelled A/B/C. Every question carries lessonId — the join key for the post-quiz review. Never match notes to questions semantically.
contentModel.lessons: Each lesson carries durationS, watchedS and thumb. thumb is null until there is real video — the tile is generated deterministically from the lesson id, so nothing looks broken and swapping in a real URL later changes nothing else. Progress is watchedS/durationS and it is the ONLY place watched state is shown. Titles never dim.
contentModel.people: initials are generated from the callsign and the avatar hue from the id, at render time. Neither is stored — one source of truth. Avatars are drawn, never uploaded: no file storage, no moderation, no cropper, and nobody has an empty avatar on day one.
contentModel.presence: Who has been on a lesson and when. Needs nobody online and is full on day one. This is what makes a room of eleven feel inhabited.

quizRules.note: Shaped after the EASA Part-66 basic examination: three alternatives labelled (A) (B) (C), one correct and two plausible-but-incomplete distractors, 75% pass mark, a nominal 75 seconds per question. 8 questions therefore reads as 'about 10 minutes' and the pass mark as '6 of 8'. NOT a real examination and the copy must never imply it is.
